title: Per-model input-length-aware SLO and token-budget reclaim protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: High variance in request input length (token count) causes skewed SLI measurements and uneven error budget consumption across models and routes. Short requests enjoy low latency while long-sequence requests disproportionately consume GPU time and burn error budgets with tail latency spikes.

Goal: Define a per-model SLO/SLI scheme that is explicit about input-length buckets, introduces a token-budget ledger for error-budget accounting, and codifies a token-budget reclaim protocol (graceful degradation + traffic shaping) that interacts with regional failover and circuit breaker policies. This ticket covers the SLO declaration format, SLI measurement rules, error-budget accounting by token-bucket, and an operational playbook for reclaiming budget when pressure is detected.

Scope:
- Design canonical SLO declaration fields for per-model, per-route, and per-input-length bucket (e.g., 0-128,129-512,513-2048,2049+).
- Define SLI computation method (weighted latency quantiles by token-segment and tail-provisioned percentiles).
- Introduce token-budget: a soft quota on total tokens served per model per error-budget window used for proactive throttles and shedding.
- Define reclaim protocol: signals, thresholds, graceful modes (prefix-cache-first, quantization-fallback, reduced-generation-length), and priority rules across tenants.
- Interaction with multi-region failover: how token-budget exhaustion in a region triggers gradual re-routing and failover priorities without violating global SLOs.
- Define observability artifacts, dashboards and alerts, and tests for canary rollouts.

Out of scope: billing or per-customer chargeback mechanics; detailed kernel-level batching optimizations (separate infra epics).
acceptance_criteria: SLO declaration schema published in Confluence with examples for at least three model archetypes (chat, completion, embedding).
Measurement implementation documented and a reference Grafana dashboard showing per-bucket SLIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability) with synthetic traffic.
Token-budget ledger prototype implemented in the trafctl service and an end-to-end flow for triggering the reclaim protocol in staging.
Failover runbook updated: when regional token-budget crosses threshold, describe incremental reroute steps and circuit-breaker interactions.
Automated tests: microbench harness that validates SLI computation against labeled traces and a postmortem playbook for budget exhaustion incidents.

Add token-budget counter & windowed aggregator to trafctl; expose API for queries and alerts

Run tabletop with SRE/PS/Support to validate runbook and handoffs

notes:
Trade-offs considered: (1) Fine-grained input buckets improve signal but risk high metric cardinality; mitigation: cap bucket tagging to top-50 models and 'other' fallback. (2) Token-budget as soft control may penalize heavy legitimate workloads—plan to surface 'grace period' and escalation to Dedicated capacity sales. (3) Interaction with quantized variants: quantized models consume less latency budget; proposal includes a conversion factor for token-budget accounting.

Open questions: exact thresholds for reclaim (suggested initial values: 70% warn, 90% soft-shed, 98% hard-shed) and tenant-priority arbitration algorithm. Need legal/enterprise input for customer-facing degradation SLAs.
